simple.meaning: דָּבַב (dâbab) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to move slowly , i.e. glide.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Song of Solomon, beginning at Song of Songs 7:10. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to דָּבַב (H1680) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.

definitions.full: H1680. dabab [ דָּבַב ] verb move Gently, glide, glide over (Late Hebrew דָּבַב flow slowly, drop ; Arabic walk leisurely, Gently , any animal that walks or creeps , compare דֹּב ; Assyrian dabâbu , plot , plan , COT Gloss , compare דִּבָּה ) — only Qal Participle יְשֵׁנִים שִׂפְתֵי דּוֺבֵב Cant 7:10, of wine gliding over the lips of sleepers ; ( ׳ד וְשִׁנָּי֑ שְׂפָתַי i.e. my lips and teeth ᵑ6 ᵐ5 Aq Gei Urschrift 405 ).
